open_risks.text: Rollback undoes itself — converge promotes whenever live differs from local main, so a rolled-back release is re-promoted at the next session start or stop unless a human also moves the main pointer back; live and unmitigated today

A PR that omits the hooks key strips every hook from live and passes validation — repo-owned absence means deletion, converge itself is removed, and permissions.deny has the identical shape, which Step 1 edits directly

validate.mjs is a syntax gate only and never executes hook logic — a behaviorally wrong permission gate promotes to live cleanly, so Layer 3 needs real behavioral tests before it merges; the pipeline will not catch a logic error

--settings accepts inline JSON, not only a file path — everything this architecture governs is file contents, so argv is an unreviewed permission-injection channel outranking project and local settings

The default sandbox configuration reports success while abandoning the sandbox — allowUnsandboxedCommands false and failIfUnavailable true are mandatory, not hardening; without them containment is illusory exactly where it matters

Unclassified settings keys land once then freeze — permissions.ask still has this shape, so introducing it even as an empty array would bind live permanently and every later repo revision would be silently inert
A merged PR does not reach live until a human advances local refs/heads/main — nothing fetches, and local main is 10 behind origin, so that advance would also drag in unrelated commits

M7 and section 10's first row still say converge promotes repo HEAD — it actually resolves the main ref and never reads HEAD, so the two coincide only when main is checked out; the amendment left this pre-existing fact alone as outside its brief

R3 names --dangerously-skip-permissions while section 5 now names --permission-mode bypassPermissions — whether these are one mechanism or two was never established, and the c10 rule change depends on that answer

key_decisions.title: D2 guards the live installed copy, not version-controlled source
The D6 checkpoint runs at the worktree root and requires --force
Allow rules enumerate narrow prefixes; a broad Bash star rule is counterproductive
Layer 0 survives on one key; the default sandbox configuration is unsafe
Oversight-reducing changes wait for direct user confirmation
Default-branch push denies stay, reclassified as delivery contract not catastrophe
